#3243. Mark Tildesley Dies: ‘No Time to Die’, ‘F1: The Movie’ & London Olympics Production Designer Was 63

Mark Tildesley, one of the industry’s most respected production designers, has passed away aged 63.

Tildesley’s many credits include James Bond movie No Time To Die, 28 Days Later, The Constant Gardener, The Two Popes, Jay Kelly, Joseph Kosinski’s F1: The Movie, and Sam Mendes’ upcoming Beatles movies. Mendes today described his collaborator as “entirely original and extraordinarily gifted”.

Tildesley’s career spanned more than three decades and he collaborated with leading filmmakers including Danny Boyle, Richard Curtis, Michael Winterbottom, Martin McDonagh, Mike Leigh, Paul Thomas Anderson, Cary Joji Fukunaga, Ron Howard, Ben Wheatley, Oliver Stone and Mendes. Related Stories News 'Sunrise On The Reaping' Firing Up Thanksgiving With $85M+ 5-Day; 'Focker In-Law' & 'Hexed' Fight For 2nd With $35M+ Apiece - Update News Michel Hazanavicius To Present Exclusive Footage Of 'The Third Hand' In AI Case Study At Les Arcs

Winterbottom and Mendes were among Tildesley’s most regular collaborators. With the former, he made seven films: I Want You, Wonderland, The Claim, 24 Hour Party People and Code 46. With the latter, he made the hit zombie film 28 Days Later, as well as Millions, Sunshine, Trance and T2 Trainspotting. Watch on Deadline

Boyle and Tildesley memorably teamed up for the 2012 London Olympics opening ceremony, a feat that earned the production designer an Emmy win alongside Suttirat Anne Larlarb.

With Mendes he made Empire Of Light and was aboard for the upcoming The Beatles — A Four-Film Cinematic Event alongside Stefania Cella and Neal Callow.

He won three British Film Designers Guild awards, for High-Rise, Empire of Light and F1: The Movie, as well as a Set Decorators Society of America prize, an Art Directors Guild award, and a British Independent Film Award.

Mendes said today: “Mark was a one-off: gentle, funny, warm, mischievous, entirely original and extraordinarily gifted. My abiding memory of him is from Empire of Light, flying down the Margate seafront on a motorised scooter, his technicolored scarf flapping in the wind, twinkling like a schoolboy playing hooky. A unique spirit and a wonderful artist. I am one of hundreds of people who are desperately sad that he is gone.”

The British Film Designers Guild (BFDG) said: “We are very sad to hear the news of Mark’s death. Besides being a well-respected and extremely talented production designer he was a friend and colleague to many of our members and will be very much missed by everyone in the Industry who knew and worked with him.”

WhatsApp is currently testing a new sticker format that plays a sound when the recipient taps on it. You can choose from a range of standard stickers as well as create your own by converting a video …

The feature was spotted by WABetaInfo in the beta version of the Android app.

WhatsApp is developing a new format to add an audio track to a sticker. This would allow users to send a sticker that plays a sound when the recipient taps it.

You can create your own audio stickers by selecting one of your videos.

Sounds don’t play automatically, but recipients will see a small audio icon attached to the sticker, and tapping it will play the sound.

#3240. This iPad Is a Lifehacker 'Gift of the Year' Award Winner, and It's $50 Off During Black Friday

If you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, you might be a bit intimidated by Apple's price tags. The iPad mini starts at $599; the base iPad Air is $749; and the entry-level iPad Pro is a whopping $1,199. Most of Apple's iPad line certainly lives up to its expensive reputation.

That's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

The iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

The iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

Apple says this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

The only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for users who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee plans to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which launched in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

But the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

That said, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

I'm not sure which I love more, the main Thanksgiving dinner or all the leftovers I get to enjoy for days afterwards. But one thing I know I don't enjoy is trying to play Tetris in my fridge to make all the food fit.

I've spent years transferring it all into tupperware, trying to make sure they stack safely, but I've always felt like I'm not making the most of my fridge space – until now. I've discovered a space-saving hack that's perfect for the holidays and here's how it works.

A post shared by Laurie (@passionatepennypincher)

On Instagram, Laurie aka @passionatepennypincher shares money-saving tips, meal-planning and practical solutions with her over 400k followers. And it's this space-saving fridge hack that she learnt from her grandma that looks like it could be a game-changer for Thanksgiving leftovers.

Instead of just having one shelf to store food, Laurie creates additional shelves above each pan and dish by using cooling racks to separate them. By placing a cooling rack in-between each layer, you're protecting the dish below from getting squashed, as well as creating a sturdy divide to stack vertically in your fridge.

This two-pack of cooling racks is surprisingly affordable, meaning each one only costs you $4.50. With that, you can create extra shelves in your fridge, as well as having a new place to cool your bakes. Perfect for the holiday season.

Immediately, I can see how this hack will save me money and time by wrapping the tops of pans with foil (or cling wrap) instead of rehoming my leftovers into bulky tupperware. And luckily, I've just bought a bunch of new cooling racks for my holiday baking, but hopefully it's a kitchen staple that most people will already have in their homes.

And while I found it to be an incredibly simple hack, stacking the pans with ease, there are a few things to be aware of. First up, you want to make sure the food is cooled before placing them on top of each other. You also want to stack the heaviest items at the bottom, just to be safe. The cooling racks are sturdy, but it's always a good idea to stack heaviest to lightest.

I also decided that since I was using foil that I'd eventually throw away, I could write on the top of it with pen to mark the date it went into the fridge. I figured if I was doing prep work on my Thanksgiving feast rather than storing leftovers, I could also write the cooking times and temperature on the foil.

#3232. Apple has iPads running macOS already, but don’t get too excited

With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A new report says that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either …

As iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but currently it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any plans to make it available outside the company.

Apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand new operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman says Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

The other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

However, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield issues may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

#3231. This Bose Portable Bluetooth Speaker Is 33% Off for Black Friday

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

A price drop always stands out more when the product in question already has a reputation for delivering above its size, and that’s the case with the Bose SoundLink Plus. It hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers.” And right now, for Black Friday, it’s down to $179, which is the lowest price we've seen.

Bose positions it right in the middle of the SoundLink lineup, and you feel that balance in how it’s built. It’s compact enough to clip onto a backpack using its built-in nylon strap, and tough enough to handle getting knocked around, and sealed against dust and full water submersion with an IP67 rating. Battery life can last up to 20 hours, depending on the volume, which is sufficient for full-day outings. On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

As for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.

#3228. How Microcredentials Can Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program pairs AI governance standards with microcredentials

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. 30 years later, 'The Birdcage' remains the ultimate survival guide for chaotic holiday dinner-table drama

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Deck the halls with family drama … fa-la-la-la-awkward. You don’t need Thanksgiving to start an argument at the dinner table, though it is the ultimate excuse to air every grievance you’ve suppressed since that doomed New Year’s resolution to "be more zen." (Spoiler alert: It didn’t stick.)

“The Birdcage” came out in 1996, yet 30 years later, it couldn’t be more relatable. Sure, it isn't marketed as a Thanksgiving movie, nor does it take place during the holiday. Still, the Robin Williams classic centers on a high-stakes family dinner showdown, serving sus soup — and plenty of political in-law drama — in bowls decked out with naked men. That kind of spice puts memaw’s pumpkin pie to shame.

The Mike Nichols-directed film is certainly a product of its time, yet nearly a decade before “Brokeback Mountain,” it did far more for LGBTQ+ inclusivity than the infamous cowboy flick.

The premise of “The Birdcage” sounds like an alpha-male podcaster’s worst nightmare: What happens when the not-so-demure daughter of a right-wing politician marries the son of a gay cabaret owner and his drag queen partner?

There’s meeting the parents, and then there’s meeting your future son-in-law’s dad and his "wife" — who happens to be Albert in drag. Robin Williams anchors the film as doting dad Armand, while Nathan Lane plays Albert, his longtime partner. Their on-screen dynamic swings from heartfelt and wholesome to wildly theatrical without ever tipping into pure parody. Dan Futterman also brings an exasperated charm to Armand’s son, groom-to-be Val — no small feat for a guy asking his dad to step back into the closet to appease his future in-laws. Not cool, Val.

The "meet the parents" trope wasn't exactly fresh in ’96; the movie was adapted from Jean Poiret’s 1973 play, “La Cage aux Folles.” Yet Gene Hackman as ultra-conservative Senator Keeley, Dianne Wiest as his wife Louise, and Calista Flockhart as bride-to-be Barbara bring an unexpected edge to a rocky family dynamic (featuring some mild repression). Even Hank Azaria (Agador) and Christine Baranski (Katharine) steal every scene they’re in. The best part? Vocally homophobic Senator Keeley seems to have a bit of a thing for Albert in a wig. Who’s going to tell him?

Beneath the farce and political clash sits a relatable story about identity, loyalty and fighting for love that hits hard during Thanksgiving and the endless gauntlet of holiday obligations that follow. Even if you think the Goldmans are way too lenient on the Keeleys (yeah, hi), it’s always easier to watch someone else’s family meltdown than to survive your own.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

You can certainly argue that “The Birdcage” isn’t perfect. It leans a little too heavily into femme stereotypes, traditional gender roles and "let's just agree to disagree" diplomacy at the queer characters' expense. Three decades on, though, it still feels like a movie that celebrates the queer community rather than treating us as the punchline, which is more than I can say for prestige dramas like “Brokeback Mountain” that double down on queer tragedy and shame. I usually champion queer stories led by creatives from the community, yet “The Birdcage” used its star-studded cast to pull mainstream audiences into an early, unapologetic celebration of queer joy.

What you take away from the movie ultimately depends on what you need. If it offers a blueprint for surviving clashing ideologies without a Thanksgiving panic attack, great. Personally, I see it as a reminder to love yourself loudly, regardless of who’s sitting across the table. Sister Sledge’s "We Are Family" plays throughout the film, but being family doesn't mean tolerating prejudice — it’s about championing a second, more vital bond: found family.

So, whether you put it on after dinner to scandalize Aunt Carol’s delicate sensibilities, or skip the family gathering altogether and protect your peace, “The Birdcage” is the exact antidote you need when you're dreading a family showdown before anyone even says grace.

New Yorkers woke up this Thanksgiving morning to drizzly, gray skies along with winds that had sidewalks covered in dead, yellow leaves, though the weather throughout the pre-noon hours was hardly the fearsome nor’easter blast that prompted the postponement till Saturday of Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade.

Still, with wind levels of up to 23 mph – and gusts considerably stronger – the postponement appears to have been justified, and the worst of the storm is yet to come.

On the Schmigadoon! IG page, Brad Oscar, dressed and in character as the Mayor, said in a video, “As mayor of Schmigadoon, I have a proclamation: The Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed until Saturday at 8:30 a.m. on NBC. See you there.”

The Book of Mormon had a simple message on its IG page about the date switch: “Ready and psyched.”

As for other non-Broadway performers originally scheduled for Thursday, reports are filtering in piecemeal on whether they’ll make the move to Saturday. The New York Post has reported that Smash Mouth will perform, and Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete are expected as well, as are the Radio City Rockettes. Other announcements should be coming in over the next day or two.

As for the marching bands, again, piecemeal reports. Texas’ Pride of Pearland Marching Band reportedly raised an extra $350,000 in community donations to cover the additional housing and transportation costs to stay until Saturday, while other marching bands were either still scrambling or had made the decision to bow out of the event due to logistics. In the latter group are the Campo Verde High School Marching Band and some members of the Bowling Green State University Marching Band that were participating in a all-star band group.

#3223. 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?

VicOne’s AI-assisted research reveals what faster zero-day discovery means for robot safety

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety.

VicOne used AI to find 28 zero-day vulnerabilities in Physical AI tools —these weaknesses can impact robot training, testing, and real-world control.

This article is brought to you by VicOne.

VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.

Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers.

Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots.

These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster, and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations.

Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. AI can accelerate parts of this work, helping researchers analyze more software in less time. Attackers could use similar capabilities.

When the weakness is a zero-day — previously unknown and without an available fix — faster discovery can leave teams with little time to respond. While that exposure does not necessarily mean an attack has occurred, teams still need to determine whether they use the affected software and what an attacker could access or change.

VicOne’s findings span three stages of the robotics lifecycle: development and training, simulation and validation, and deployment and runtime. Weaknesses at each stage could affect what a robot learns, how it is tested, and how it is controlled.

Figure 1. In this research set, 75% of findings involved development, training, simulation, or validation tools, highlighting risks that can arise before a robot is deployed.VicOne

The following scenarios show how a compromised component could influence the robot at each stage.

These are potential consequences and not demonstrated outcomes for every finding. Actual effects depend on the attacker’s access, the system’s design, and whether other safeguards prevent the changes from reaching physical behavior.

In a separate demonstration, VicOne researchers provide a concrete example of a weakness affecting a protective function. The researchers exploited a vulnerability to prevent a robot’s remote-stop command from working. The case shows why teams need to test whether safeguards remain effective when the software supporting them is compromised.

Video 1. VicOne researchers demonstrate a vulnerability that prevents a robot’s remote-stop command from working. VicOne

AI can shorten the search for weaknesses, but a robotics team still needs to determine whether a fix is safe to deploy. Even after a software maintainer releases a patch, teams must identify affected systems, check compatibility, and verify that the update preserves intended behavior.

An earlier successful test remains useful evidence. However, a newly discovered weakness may reveal conditions that test never examined.

When immediate updating is impractical, teams may need temporary safeguards, such as restricting access to an affected service, while a validated fix is prepared.

As details from the 28 findings become available through coordinated disclosure, the next step is for robotics manufacturers is to connect each finding to its potential effect on development, deployment, and robot behavior.

That work also requires understanding how threats could affect robot behavior and how to protect systems already in operation. VicOne Radeis helps teams identify potential zero-day vulnerabilities, assess AI model and system security, and use simulation to evaluate how these risks could affect robot behavior before deployment. VicOne Rthena supports threat detection and responses within approved policies during operation.

Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne

Faster vulnerability discovery matters when teams can turn findings into action: identify what needs attention, verify that safeguards still hold, and confirm that a fix does not introduce new risks. That is how cybersecurity strengthens robot safety as systems continue to change.

For a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper, “Why Robot Safety Depends on Cybersecurity: Protecting the Information That Safety Decisions Rely On.”

I know the TV world can be super overwhelming — trust me, I’ve been there. So let’s do a quick rundown of the differences between the three “premium” panel types.

So an OLED has lots of mini diodes inside the panel that emit light individually. This means there’s no backlight, unlike older TVs. This means OLEDs are better for higher contrast, better blacks, better color, and smooth motion for gaming.

QLEDs also use a light-emitting diode. Unlike OLED, a QLED panel has a backlight, which illuminates each diode individually. QLEDs are better for brighter rooms, as the panel itself tends to be brighter, but OLEDs can reach better contrast levels and color accuracy.

Mini-LED is something else entirely: it uses tiny LEDs (light-emitting diodes, like both QLED and OLED) — but thousands of them. That means each diode can pack a major color and brightness punch. Mini-LEDs can be brighter, blacker, and more colorful — all at once.

#3218. New Book Alleges Former Disney Chief Bob Iger Impregnated Employee Leading To “Traumatic Termination Procedure”

A bombshell book about former Disney boss Bob Iger alleges that the exec impregnated an underling employee in the early 1990s that resulted in “a traumatic termination procedure.”

Details of the book went public in a New York Times article today.

The New York Times report, which features excerpts from The House of Mouse by Wall Street Journal reporter Robbie Whelan, was published in the paper and claims that a consensual extramarital relationship between Iger and a woman described as an “ABC marketer” resulted in a pregnancy. Related Stories News UK Actors Union Equity To Kickstart Negotiations With Streamers Early Next Year Sports Imax To Screen Super Bowl In Deal With Disney, NFL

In his new book, Whelan, according to The Times, “contrasts Mr. Iger’s public support for the #MeToo movement in the late 2010s with an extramarital relationship he had with an ABC marketer in the early 1990s.” Whelan “points to a power imbalance: Mr. Iger, then running ABC Entertainment, was rungs above her. The woman became pregnant and ‘suffered through a traumatic termination procedure.'” Watch on Deadline

Whelan has defended the inclusion of the episode in his book as an example of the “disconnect between Mr. Iger’s public principles and private conduct.”

According to Whelen, the 75-year-old Iger declined to be interviewed for The House of Mouse, but “enlisted a lawyer who sent letters to the publisher raising concerns about a potentially ‘false and defamatory’ account.” Disney also declined to cooperate, Whelan said, adding “Their instinct was to bully me.”

Disney had no comment when contacted today by Deadline.

Disney did provide a statement to The Times, but did not directly address Whelan’s claim about the affair. “Bob Iger is one of the most respected C.E.O.s of his generation,” the company said, citing, among other things, his “bold creative and strategic decisions” and saying he left Disney “stronger and more innovative.” A representative for Iger declined the Times’ request for comment.

Elsewhere in today’s article, the Times writes that The House of Mouse depicts Iger “as insecure, vindictive and preoccupied with money.”

“I am frustrated about compensation!” Iger wrote in one of several private emails obtained by Whelan. “I had a nasty and distasteful negotiation to extend my contract this last time.” The 2014 message went to Ike Perlmutter, then Marvel’s chairman and a major Disney shareholder.

HarperCollins releases The House of Mouse on December 1 – the same day Iger is scheduled to attend his final Disney board meeting.

#3217. Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement



In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

What You Will Learn:

  • How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processes
  • How baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affected
  • How in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structures
  • When offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign material
  • How correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projects

The PS5 Black Friday deals are officially live, and we're tracking every price drop across Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, Target, GameStop and PlayStation Direct as they happen.

With GTA 6 driving huge demand and keeping official PS5 and PS5 Pro console discounts rare this year, finding real value means knowing where to look.

Right now, the biggest savings are on accessories, games and certified refurbished consoles — including $54 DualSense controllers, PS5 slim systems from $499 refurbished and PS5 games starting from as little as $10.

Plus, we know the best places to look (even places your AI agent is probably never going to go). So keep us bookmarked and follow along. Here are the best Black Friday PS5 deals you can buy right now.

Stellar Blade is a hack-and-slash action-adventure game in the best spirit of the genre. It takes full advantage of the PS5's horsepower and serves up thrilling combat sequences and an engaging story. The graphics aren't half bad-looking, either.

Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor thanks to its larger scope, both narratively and gameplay-wise. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer a deep level of customization.

Sony’s standard PS5 pad remains one of the best controllers around thanks to its responsive haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Standard colorways, including white, midnight black, cosmic red, and galactic purple, are down to $54 here, beating PlayStation Direct’s sale price.

The Razer Raiju V3 Pro's TMR sticks offer precise control over movements while removing the risk of stick drift, and the gamepad’s Hall Effect triggers are fantastic too. The controller is highly customizable with removable back buttons and personalization via Windows and/or mobile software.

Sony's first set of PlayStation wireless earbuds, the Pulse Explore, are discounted this Black Friday. These are a great pick if you don't want to wear a bulky over-ear headset while playing multiplayer games.

The PS5 is hard to come by this Black Friday, and if you do find one, it's at retail. That stings, but it doesn't hurt to get a PS5 when you can. This model is the base PS5 Slim, now the cheapest PS5 available. It comes with an 825GB SSD.

If you haven’t played Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 yet, it’s easy to recommend - especially since you can save $22 at Target right now.

This superhero sequel takes place after the original and the standalone Miles Morales title, and sees Peter Parker reunited with his best pal Harry Osborn, crossing paths with Kraven the Hunter, and encountering a strange black goo.

Spider-Man 2 tells a great story, but it’s also a great showcase for the PS5 since it looks amazing in motion, and you can instantly swap between Peter and Miles. We awarded it 4.5 stars in our review.

Handing another Marvel character to the team at Insomniac Games felt like a surefire way to success, but Wolverine didn’t live up to the standard set by the studio’s three Spider-Man titles.

And yet, if you’ve been curious and are in the mood for some adamantium-coated ultraviolence, you can save 29% on Marvel’s Wolverine at Amazon.

We gave it 3.5 stars in our review, but if you’re looking for a linear action title to show off your PS5 console, you could do a lot worse.

Not to be outdone by the Xbox Elite Controller, Sony launched the DualSense Edge. It features all of the features you’d expect from a first-party PlayStation 5 controller, like adaptive triggers and haptic rumble.

What the Edge adds is, well, an Edge - competitively speaking. Swappable thumbstick caps for your preferred feel, reprogrammable back buttons so you don’t need to move your fingers off the triggers in your favorite shooter, and the option to create profiles on PS5 and PC.

It’s still more expensive than the standard DualSense, but you can get one for $169 right now.

Inarguably one of PS5’s most chaotic multiplayer titles, Helldivers 2 is a ridiculously fun time with friends.

Players drop into a variety of planets to fight robots, bugs, and more in a third-person shooter homage to Starship Troopers, but the best part is how it feels like a storytelling engine. You’ll never forget the time you accidentally shot down a buddy who walked in your line of fire, or accidentally dropped an airstrike on your squad’s heads.

You can spread Managed Democracy for just $30 at Walmart right now, a discount of almost ten bucks.

Another of the current crop of sports games, EA SPORTS FC 27 is perfect if you’re still in the grip of World Cup fever.

This year’s title introduces a collection mechanic to Ultimate Team that has you rewarded for racking up themed sets, as well as major improvements to transfers in Career Mode. Dynamic OVR also means players will improve if they’re in form, giving you some selection headaches.

As with NBA 2K27, it’s now under $30 at just $29.95 - a 57% discount on the MSRP.

NBA 2K27 only launched a few weeks ago, but the series is always good for a Black Friday saving.

That’s exactly what Amazon is offering, with the best-looking sports sim around reduced to under $30 for the Standard Edition on PS5. As you’d expect, it’s an evolution rather than a revolution year-on-year, but there are improvements to animations, female MyPLAYERs, and new MyCAREER Eras to explore.

It’s a basketball sandbox, and it’s better than half price.

Sony hasn’t launched a handheld since the ill-fated PlayStation Vita, but the PlayStation Portal might be the next best thing.

Capable of remote streaming while out and about, and streaming from your home console while you’re indoors, it’s an ideal way to play games like Grand Theft Auto 6 without taking up the whole telly (although, if you’re anything like me, your wife insists on watching it like it’s a crime drama TV show).

This deal nets you the Portal, as well as a handy accessories kit including a charging dock, carry case, outer shell, earbuds, and a screen protector at a $35 discount.

Another 2022 hit, Gran Turismo 7 saw Sony’s Polyphony Digital studio roar back with a racing sim that has some of the most stunningly detailed car models you’ll ever see - and it’s seeing a big discount at Target.

So good-looking that you’ll want to reach out and touch the steering wheel, the game is still getting updates to include new cars, tracks, and quality-of-life features.

Our reviewer awarded it 4.5 stars out of 5 in our review, and it’s only gotten better since then - particularly if you have a PS5 Pro.

It’s hard to believe it’s been nearly five years since it launched, but Elden Ring remains one of the best games ever made - and a must-play on PS5.

If you’ve picked up a console just for GTA 6 and missed out on this fantasy action-RPG, you can snag it for just $15 right now at Amazon.

It’s challenging, yes, but it’s also unforgettable. In fact, the PS5 version has a colossal 96-percent positive rating on Metacritic.

If you're a multi-platform gamer, this one is for you. The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni headset is currently $50 off at Amazon. The "Omni" in its name stands for two things: firstly it has an omni-directional mic for more natural vocal tones; secondly, it's compatible with PC, PS5 and Xbox. You can hook up to all three at once via USB for hi-res audio and simply switch between inputs as you need to. So handy.

As I noted in my SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni review, the sound quality is also excellent, the headset is super comfy and it features a zero downtime battery system with one battery charging in the USB hub as you use the other in the headset.

There's no shortage of games on sale today, including $10 off Assassin's Creed: Shadows at Amazon. "The best entry in the franchise since the good ol’ days of Ezio," is what our reviewer gave in her 4.5* Assassin's Creed: Shadows review. "Feudal Japan looks gorgeous and is brimming with activity and idle chatter, while the story itself is compelling... It’s even better than I’d hoped and I was fully invested after just a few hours of play."

The PlayStation Pulse Explore gaming earbuds have hit their lowest ever price for Black Friday, reduced from $199 to $119 at Amazon — a huge $80 saving. We gave these buds four stars in our PlayStation Pulse Explore review. We loved the immersive in-game sound and fantastic fidelity. There's multipoint connectivity so you can hook up to your phone, too.

If you often play at night and want to be able to fully enjoy the sound of your games without waking your family or neighbors, this is the deal for you.

Why not round out your setup with a shiny new TV? One of our favorite deals overall right now is on the TCL QM6K 75-inch 4K Mini-LED TV, which is currently over $300 off at Amazon. We gave this TV four stars in our review, and it's been a favorite of ours to recommend for a while now in the sub-$1,000 category. At just $697 with this deal, it's positively a steal.

Importantly, on top of its excellent picture quality, it features a 144Hz refresh rate, so you can max out that PS5 at 120fps. If you're playing GTA VI though, obviously, you'll only need 30 of those frames.

You can also follow our Black Friday TV deals coverage for more great TV deals.

When it comes to Star Wars games on PS5, most people will wax lyrical about Galactic Racer or Jedi Survivor, and don't get me wrong, both deserve their flowers, they're great games, but so is Star Wars Zero Company. Don't let it be forgotten!

Now on sale for $44 on Amazon, in this turn-based tactics game, you control the titular squad, a scrappy group of mercs and misfits, roped into a dangerous mission with high stakes. I'm not usually one for tactics games, but Zero Company really hooked me at launch because of its accessible combat design and its focus on player choice. If you play with "permadeath" switched on (and you should), squad members can die for good in battle, which means every decision you make feels important. There's a wealth of content and loads of ways to customize your team.

It's always useful to have an extra DualSense controller, either for co-op gaming or so you can switch between a couple to make sure you always have a fully charged pad.

Right now, PS5 DualSense controllers start at $54 on Amazon. This deal isn't just on the stock white model, but also on other color options like the slick Midnight Black. Or if you don't mind spending a little extra, for $64 you can get very funky designs such as the Rhythm Blue, Techno Red, or Remix Green.

So far, I've been sharing great deals on games I've already played (and enjoyed), but here's one I'm tempted to pick up for myself, on a title missed earlier this year.

Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is now $39 at Amazon. The prequel to the excellent Plague Tale games launched in August, during a crowded release period, so I didn't have time to play it over the summer. But I've heard great things, and as a fan of the Plague Tale series, this discount is just the nudge I need to circle back. Though I'll likely buy it and put it in my backlog, which is already overflowing.

Perhaps in an attempt to pry gamers away from Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest Call of Duty game, Modern Warfare 4, is on sale for $54 at Amazon — a $15 discount.

While very much the standard Call of Duty experience, that's not a bad thing, MW4 offers a rich suite of modes, with a single-player campaign, a new DMZ extraction mode, and the dependable range of competitive online modes. Shooting is zippy, as always with CoD, and new updates are rolling out at a constant clip, so there's always a new map to try or a new weapon or perk to unlock.

It doesn't reinvent the Call of Duty series by any stretch, but it serves up reliable FPS entertainment, and sometimes that's all you want out of a new online shooter.

The recently released Ghost of Yotei Complete Edition is $49 at Best Buy, a $20 saving on this package, which bundles the full GoY base game, the Echoes of Sekigahara single-player expansion, the Most Wanted survival mode, and the Legends online co-op mode. It's a whole lot of Ghost of Yotei at a reduced price.

It's not just the PS5 Pro suffering from stock issues this holiday season; the regular PS5 is also becoming very tough to find at MSRP. The likes of Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart are sold out, but at GameStop, you can get a PS5 Slim Digital Edition for $599 (aka its regular price). Meanwhile, if you're okay with a refurbished model, you can get a refurbished PS5 starting from $499 over on PlayStation Direct.

Saros is sort of like Sony's forgotten exclusive this year. Which is a real shame because, as I said in my Saros review, it's "a relentless, exciting and demanding rogue-lite shooter that combines cinematic spectacle with tight bullet-hell combat."

The spiritual sequel to 2021's Returnal, Saros is on sale for $39 (was $69), a great price for a thrilling bullet-hell shooter that deserved more attention at launch back in the spring. If you skipped it, then this deal is an excuse to fix that oversight.

During my time at Tom's Guide, I've reviewed dozens of PS5 games, The Last of Us Part II Remastered is one of only two I've given a full five-star score. Right now, you can pick up The Last of Us Part II Remastered for $27 (44% off) over on Amazon.

Did The Last of Us Part II need remastering? Maybe not. The original PS4 version still looks amazing to this day and plays perfectly on PS5, but if you've never experienced this modern masterpiece, this is the version to get. Aside from a few minor visual upgrades, you get new content like the addictive No Return mode, which puts a roguelike spin on TLOU 2's excellent combat. It's a PS5 game everybody should play!

If you demand value-for-money in your next PS5 purchase, the Kingdom Hearts Collection [I-III] for $59 (was $74) on Amazon is a deal you shouldn't ignore.

It offers the entire Kingdom Hearts saga to date (bar the Melody of Memory spin-off title released in 2020) in a single package. That's all 3 mainline games (and KH 3's DLC) and 7 interstitial titles (3 of which have been converted into HD movies). There's so much content here; you'll probably still be working through it all by the time Kingdom Hearts 4 launches in late 2027.

As a recent convert to the Kingdom Hearts series thanks to the very collection, I'm really enjoying my time so far, and this package makes for the ideal starting point.

If the wait until The Witcher 4 is getting you down, grab The Blood of Dawnwalker for $30 at Amazon (57% off its MSRP of $69). It's an RPG that wears its Witcher inspiration on its sleeve, probably because it was developed by ex-Witcher devs.

You play Coen, a young man on a quest to save his family from a ruthless vampire lord, who has become a Dawnwalker (essentially human by day, vampire at night). What makes this one special, aside from the strong quest writing and focus on player choice, is the day/night cycle. Completing quests or side activities moves the in-game clock forward, so you have to spend your time wisely. Waste it, and your family will meet a grisly fate. This mechanism adds real weight to every decision.

The DualSense Edge is the "pro" version of the stock PS5 DualSense controller, and for Black Friday it's on sale for $169 at Amazon, which is a solid $30 discount.

To justify its premium price, you get swappable stick modules, mappable back buttons, adjustable trigger lengths, and fully customizable button profiles. Plus, because it's a PlayStation product, it still includes adaptive triggers and haptic feedback — features that third-party pro controllers are forced to omit.

It has been cheaper during previous Black Friday sales (it's dropped to $149 in the past), but $169 is the lowest price I've spotted in 2026, so it's worth considering.

The mark of a good survival horror is if it sticks around in your psyche for weeks (even months) afterward, and that's definitely been the case with Silent Hill Townfall.

In my review, I called this "one of the most intense games I've ever played," and I stand by it. Set in a remote Scottish town and the first full Silent Hill game played in first-person, it's a nightmare experience, full of horrific sights and a bleak, dark atmosphere. It also looks stunning on PS5 and offers a cryptic but compelling story.

For Black Friday, Silent Hill Townfall is on sale for $29, down from its launch price of $49. That's a bargain price, particularly because with 5 unlockable endings, you'll probably want to play this game multiple times. Assuming you have the nerve for it.

Resident Evil Requiem is one of the best games released in 2026, and in my opinion, the best entry in the series when it comes to balancing horror and action. This is because of the dual protagonist setup, casting you as both fan-favorite Leon S. Kennedy and newcomer Grace Ashcroft. Leon's section is pure action, while Grace's really ramps up the fear. It's the best of both styles. It's also playable in both first and third person, or a mix of the two (which is the ideal way to play).

I'd recommend Resi 9 at full price, and did as much back in February when it launched. So, it's no surprise that I'm even more eager to encourage you to pick up now that it's more than 40% off ahead of Black Friday over on Amazon.

Hey all, I'm Rory, one of the biggest gamers on staff at Tom's Guide (and a 30+ year PlayStation fan), here to guide you through the next few hours of PS5 deal coverage.

Let's start with talking PS5 Pro. The souped-up PlayStation console has been in high demand this year, largely due to the launch of a certain GTA 6, so I've been tracking PS5 Pro restocks the last couple of months. While the console remains out of stock across major retailers even a week post-GTA 6's launch, I'm hoping that Black Friday itself could bring more stock. Surely, there will be restocks this side of the holidays?

I'll keep monitoring retailer listing, and report back if I catch sight of any stock, but if you want to check for yourself, below are all the retailer links you need right now.

Whether your original DualSense is at the end of its life or you want a second because you just bought a couch co-op game, you're in luck. The DualSense is discounted by $20 right now, so you can get one (or two... or three) for just $54 at Amazon.

Sony’s standard PS5 pad remains one of the best controllers around thanks to its responsive haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Standard colorways, including White, Midnight Black, Cosmic Red, and Galactic Purple, are down to $54 at Amazon, beating PlayStation Direct’s sale price.

Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart is a stellar game for PS5 owners, and one that's so addicting that I didn't even realize it was 3AM when I was playing it. With its incredibly fun gameplay, satisfying balanced story, gorgeous graphics and music, and excellent use of PS5 features, you'll feel the same way.

Games, of course, don't always come cheap, and if you've been holding off on buying Rift Apart, time to hit "add to cart" now. It's discounted by 57% so you can get it for just $29 at Amazon right now.

So, this is one deal I've personally got my eye on because I'm thinking of getting it. Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is down to $54 at Amazon right now, and well-worth it for anyone who wants to live out their fighter pilot dreams.

The latest installment in the storied franchise boasts a full single-player campaign and the series' largest suite of online modes to date. With stunning visuals and sounds, it's the complete package — and this Black Friday deal doesn't break the bank either!

"Why do we fall, sir? So that we can learn to pick ourselves up. Batman begin," is what Michael Caine tweeted a couple years ago. He forgot the "s" at the end, and every time I think of the tweet, I laugh out loud. The tweet naturally went viral, and it even made its way into Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight.

That's enough reason to buy the game this Black Friday, which is down to $49 at Amazon.

Oh, you need more reasons? Fiiiiine. Lego Batman is extremely fun. It takes everything folks know about Batman from popular culture and filters it through the tried-and-true Lego formula. You'll love it.

I absolutely adore animals — sometimes I think I might like them more than humans, actually. If you're like me, you should play Planet Zoo, which is down to $32 at Amazon for Black Friday. I myself bought the game during last year's sale!

Those who played Zoo Tycoon back in the day will be familiar with how Planet Zoo works. In this wildlife park management sim, you build enclosures for your animals, look after them to ensure they're happy, and also keep up your guests' happiness and satisfaction levels. It's really, really fun.

Whether you've played the 1997 Final Fantasy VII or are a newcomer to the series, boy have I found some killer deals for you. Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade is a whopping 63% off right now so you can get it for $14, and its sequel, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is also available for $14.

Remake Intergrade is a stunning game with excellent music, fun combat, a compelling storyline, and versatile playable characters. Rebirth is also a phenomenal JRPG thanks to its stellar graphics, robust customization options, and vast explorable environments.

Both games are must-play for PS5 owners, and the perfect way to pass the time until Final Fantasy VII Revelation comes out in 2027!

The DualSense is my favorite controller. Its haptic feedback and adaptive triggers deliver a truly immersive experience unlike any other. If you want to experience the full extent of the DualSense's capabilities, you need to play Astro Bot. Right now, it's down to $37 at Amazon.

"One of the best PlayStation games ever," is how we described it in our 4.5-star review of Astro Bot. This is a truly joyful platforming experiences that's elevated by its inventive level design and countless loving nods to PlayStation's rich history.

Trust me, this game will make you fall in love with the DualSense (if you aren't already).

Ghost of Yotei is one of the best PS5 exclusives of all time, and if you're a fan of Ghost of Tsushima, you need to play the sequel. In GoY, you play as Atsu, a female mercenary hunting down the Yōtei Six to avenge her family in 1603 Ezo.

In this highly cinematic single-player game, you embark on a visually beautiful journey with a compelling storyline. The massive open-world is stuffed full of activities, like petting foxes and defending wolf dens, and the music is just as gorgeous.

Right now, you can get the Complete Edition (including the Most Wanted DLC and Sekigahara story expansion) for just $49 at Amazon.

You can't play Mario Kart on the PS5 but Sonic Racing CrossWorlds is the next best thing — and it honestly makes MK look like child's play. It's one of the most memorable entries in the Sonic the Hedgehog series, and is a must-have for racing fans.

Packed with chaos, fun and presenting a bit of a learning curve, CrossWorlds wins big when it comes to smooth drifting and air tricks that give you significant boosts. Extensive kart and ‘Gadget Plate’ customization enable you to strategize in different ways and fine-tune your style.

If you fancy picking up a new racing game just in time for the holidays, Sonic Racing CrossWorlds is down to just $19 at Amazon — that's 50% off!

Fancy over-ear headphones instead? The Razer BlackShark V3 Pro is my current go-to headset — and one of the very few products I've awarded 5/5 stars to. I'd recommend these cans even at their full price, but you can grab them for just $199 at Amazon (their lowest ever price).

The BlackShark V3 Pro "makes me feel like I’m playing video games at the movie theater." That's how I described the sound quality in my review. These cans boast fantastic sound with spatial audio support that gives you a competitive edge. With highly effective ANC, you can truly feel like the main character.

Alongside controllers, I also test gaming headsets (I know, I have a very cool job). That includes headphones and earbuds designed specifically for the PlayStation. If you want a pair of earbuds that look uber cool and sound even better, I recommend the Sony PlayStation Pulse Explore.

When I reviewed them, I knocked a point off because of their high price — no more, though, as the earbuds are $80 off right now, so you can get them for just $119 at Amazon!

The Pulse Explore boast immersive in-game audio thanks to the planar magnetic drivers, while the fully customizable 3D audio profiles and multipoint connectivity truly elevate your gaming experience. They’re also extremely comfortable to wear during long gaming sessions.

I love Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order, but I love its sequel, Survivor, even more... and I wasn't expecting to see such a massive discount on it today! You can save $59 on Star Wars Jedi Survivor today as the game is down to just $10 at the PlayStation Store.

In Survivor, you play as Cal Kestis, accompanied by his trusted droid BD-1, as he continues his ongoing battle against the Galactic Empire and his quest to reunite the surviving Jedi. Thanks to satisfying lightsaber combat and fluid gameplay, as well as stunning graphics, Survivor is a must-play for Star Wars fans and casuals alike.

As you can probably tell by now, I'm an avid gamer. Thing is, my partner isn't. So I embarked on a simple mission: find couch co-op games that aren't overly complicated so that she can see how fun video games can be. That's when I found Unravel Two.

Unravel Two is a story-driven side-scrolling game where you and your partner play as a pair of adorable protagonists called Yarnies. A mix of chase sequences and platforming make it a wonderful game, and there's a compelling and beautiful storyline will be tugging on your heartstrings.

If, like me, you've got a loved one you really want to play games with, Unravel Two is the perfect starting point — and you can grab it for just $4 today!

5/5 star ratings are extremely rare at Tom's Guide, and 007 First Light is one of the only games we've awarded it to. It serves as the perfect origin story for James Bond, and it's the best 007 game since Golden Eye. As someone who'd fallen out of love with Bond, it made me care about the franchise again.

007 First Light's cinematic single-player campaign is "remarkable, offering a gripping, quintessentially Bond story, packaged together with some of the best action-adventure set pieces I’ve ever experienced." That's how our reviewer, Rory, described the game in his review. High praise!

This is a game you need to experience for yourself — and now you can, thanks to this Black Friday discount. 007 First Light is available for $34 at PlayStation right now.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is the 2026 remake of the 2013 hit game — and one that's loved by many fans. This Black Friday deal is too good to ignore, as it drops the game's price by 50%!

Black Flag Resynced is a wonderful remake. It looks gorgeous, adds worthwhile new content that adds to Edward Kenway's story, and makes loads of smart improvements. If you want to ignore the main story and do nothing but sail the stunning seas, go deep sea diving, be my guest. Being a ruthless pirate has never been this fun.

Assassin's Creed is one of my favorite franchises, and I've played every single entry in the series. Right now, many of them are down to their lowest ever prices across Amazon and the PlayStation Store. If you've been meaning to sink your teeth into one, now's the time.

For example, Assassin's Creed Origins (set in ancient Egypt) is down to just $8 at PlayStation — it usually costs $59!

I'm not a huge fan of horror games as I chicken out too quickly — but Alan Wake 2 is a game I keep coming back to. The Deluxe Edition (which includes the Night Springs and Lake House DLCs) is available for just $29 at Amazon right now.

Alan Wake 2 weaves together two compelling protagonists across a unique, multi-dimensional, narrative that is often seriously strange but still surprisingly engrossing. You solve various puzzles, take down different kinds of enemies with your flashlight and guns, and untangle the Dark Place's mystery.

Oh, and there's a fun musical number in there, too, and that alone makes the game worth playing!

Black Friday is the best time to pick up a new game, yes, but it's also the perfect time to pick up a new controller. As part of my job as a senior reviews writer, I test the best controllers for PC and consoles — and the Razer Raiju V3 Pro is one of my favorites for PS5.

The Raiju V3 Pro features TMR thumbsticks that offer precise control over movements while removing the risk of stick drift. Then you've got Hall Effect triggers that are highly responsive and customizable. The back buttons are removable, and personalization via the mobile app is quick and easy.

The only things you miss out with the Raiju V3 Pro are adaptive triggers and haptic feedback — which is the case with most third-party PS5 controllers. Small price to pay if you value precision over everything else, though, right? Right now, it's down to $156 from $219 at Amazon.

It's great that lots of AAA games are discounted for Black Friday, but if you want a cozy, easy-to-play game, I've got a fantastic recommendation for you. Neva is currently 50% off at the PlayStation Store right now, so you can get it for just $9.

Neva is a puzzle-platformer with barely any dialog, where the beautiful art design and stunning music do the talking for the game. It conveys a lovely story which you only understand when you reach the end, and it may drive you to tears — I sobbed like a baby.

Hello, one and all! Nikita here, taking over from Jason. I've just earned the Platinum trophy in Control Resonant so that's the first game I'm going to convince you to buy this Black Friday. Right now, it's down to $49 at Amazon — I'd even recommend buying it at full price so this is a steal!

As someone who loved the original Control, Resonant surpasses my expectations. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging; the soundtrack is immaculate; Dylan (the protagonist) is compelling as are the supporting characters; and the skill tree and various traversal abilities you can acquire are nothing like you've seen before.

Regardless of whether you're a fan of Remedy's games or not, this is a game you shouldn't skip. After spending over 60 hours with Resonant, it's my personal Game of the Year (GTA 6 who?).

I've played a lot of racing games this year, and out of all the arcade titles, I didn't expect Star Wars: Galactic Racer to be an absolute banger!

The premise is simple — a rogue-like kind of title where you blitz through different sets of races on different planets, randomized every time you go through with new upgrades as you go.

That's a nice tactical dimension added to what is some phenomenal racing gameplay. It takes me back to seeing Anakin in Episode One every time: the high-stakes competition rushing by at 400 MPH, the combat of it all. It is phenomenal.

Trust me, it's worthy of your $49 right now.

The audacity! I'm only in my mid-30s, but apparently one of my favorite games of 2026 is a "dad game"!? I feel like I just aged 10 years reading that sentence.

Oh...on a second read, turns out he's talking about how it's playing a Father-like figure in-game...I'll pass my apologies to Scott (may have got a little frustrated at him.

In that vein, he's absolutely right. It's a great little duo relationship between you two that connects on an emotional level — paired with unique sci-fi gameplay that is easy to get addicted to.

Read our Pragmata review, where we called it the surprise hit for 2026, and save $20 on it right now.

Silent Hill: Townfall is easily the best the series has been in 25 years. Screen Burn’s shift to first-person and a bleak, remote Scottish town breathes massive new life into the franchise, all while keeping its trademark atmosphere, visuals, and skin-crawling sound design completely intact. It’s properly horrific, genuinely unsettling, and I never wanted to stop playing.

Yes, just like the parody on GTA 6, this is indeed the remaster of the remake of The Last of Us. Chances are a lot of you have already played it!

But if you haven't (or you haven't played this version), the huge improvement in visual fidelity, animation and gameplay with more aggressive enemies and an increased focus on tactics, makes it well worth revisiting.

Also, well worth noting that this is without a doubt the best story ever told in gaming. There's a reason I have a tattoo dedicated to the game after all!

I mean GTA 6 is 212GB, and that's not even the worst of it (looking at you, Call of Duty). Today's games take up a lot of storage, and if you're reliant on the on-board space, you're going to fill that up fast.

That's why adding an SSD to your PS5 is becoming essential, and one of the best I've tested in terms of zippy speeds and strong sustained performance is actually one of the smallest.

The Sandisk Optimus GX 7100M can read/write just as fast as the onboard storage (GTA 6 loads within a few milliseconds of the time on SSD as it takes on the internal storage). And you can get $87 off it right now!

If your place is a little too cramped for a soundbar or surround sound speakers, a decent headset is the best way to really enhance the audio experience of Leonida as you play GTA 6.

And my personal favorites come from Nacon — the RIG R5 Spear for a wired option and the R8 Spectre Pro for a wireless afair.

The all-encompassing surround sound is seriously impressive (especially for the price you can get them now) with great attention to the finer details and nicely booming bass.

Right now, you can save big on both headsets, which gives you enough money leftover for these custom faceplates that give your cans a GTA flavor!

If you haven't tried this Miyazaki masterpiece that has won a whole bunch of game awards, you literally have no excuse now.

For the price of your average McDonald's meal, you can snag one of the best Soulslike games from the maker of Dark Souls — massive in scope, glorious in combat.

And at this price? It's one of those "don't even think about it" kind of deals to just snag right now.

So Wolverine is Insomniac's newest game, but its not their best. I'm torn between Ratchet & Clank and this masterpiece: Marvel's Spider-Man 2.

There's honestly nothing more satisfying gameplay wise than webbing your way across the city and fighting crime. Plus the storyline here is incredibly gripping and visually, it's stunning.

If you haven't got round to picking it up, it's 57% off right now. That is an absolute steal on this game!

So I bought Marvel's Wolverine at launch. Personally, I love it. It's no Spider-Man (more on that later as that is also discounted too), and at its full $69 price given the size and scope of it, I can appreciate that some folks may not be the biggest fans.

However, with $20 off? This is where it becomes a much more tantalizing prospect to become Logan and get super violent. It's a great story, looks incredible and the combat feels very satisfying.

So let me start with the bad news — the PS5 Pro is either out of stock or being scalped on the used market. If you see one of these for anything more than $1,000, do not buy.

Now to the good news for those who are keen to get in on the GTA 6 hype, but don't have the box to play it: there is PS5 stock available to grab! PlayStation's own certified refurbished program has some decently-priced systems, and GameStop has a brand new units too.

And yes, Walmart technically has the PS5 digital Slim too, but for $900!? Hell no.

Gran Turismo 7 plays great on a controller of course! But to really get the best out of it, you're going to need a racing wheel.

Yes, there is the Logitech G923 bundle for $120 off, but you'll be doing yourself a disservice with this one. It's a gear-driven wheel (using gears inside to identify steering movements and provide force feedback), which means it's not the most reliable and the feedback you get is week.

But that's where the Thrustmaster T598 comes in — arguably one of my favorite value racing wheels of the past few years. You get surprisingly strong direct drive and a great feel in a compact package.

And right now, it's also $120 off. The price is a little more than the Logitech, but it's so worth it for the night and day difference.

As you may already know about me, I'm the motor racing guy on the team — addicted to sim racing, and realizing just how different the real thing is.

One of the games that has stuck with me throughout my three decades of PlayStation gaming is Gran Turismo, and the 7th edition has had me hooked for hundreds of hours.

If you haven't played it yet, you owe it to yourself to get it for this dirt cheap price of $29!

I'll be sharing some of my favorite games on sale, accessories to really enhance your time playing and keeping a close eye on any console stock I find (as well as some personal tips).
